title: Circuits and Switches
seo_title: Year 6 Science: Circuits and Switches Worksheets (Will It Work? Conductors and Faults)
standard_text: Compare and give reasons for variations in how components function, including the brightness of bulbs, the loudness of buzzers and the on/off position of switches.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 science worksheets on circuits and switches: complete circuits, open and closed switches, two switches in series, conductors and insulators, and finding faults. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: A complete loop with a cell and closed switches makes components work.
body_html:
How to think about it

A component works only in a complete loop that has a cell and no gaps.

  • A closed switch completes the loop; an open switch makes a gap. With two switches in one loop, both must be closed.
  • Metals conduct electricity; plastic, rubber, wood and glass are insulators.
  • If something does not work, check the cells, the bulb, each connection, the switches and the materials.
Example

Two switches in a loop: one open, one closed. Lamp?

The open switch makes a gap

Answer: off

Example

A plastic ruler across a gap. Lamp?

Plastic is an insulator

Answer: off

Common mistakes

  • Thinking one closed switch is enough when there are two in the loop.
  • Thinking plastic can complete a circuit.
  • Forgetting that cells run out.

faq.q: Why does a switch turn a lamp off?
faq.a: Opening the switch makes a gap in the circuit, so current cannot flow around the loop and the lamp goes out.

faq.q: What happens with two switches in one circuit?
faq.a: If both are in the same loop (in series), both must be closed for the lamp to light. Opening either one breaks the circuit.
Check that the cell is not flat, the bulb is not blown, every wire is firmly connected, the switch is closed and nothing in the loop is an insulator.
